operations.title: WP24b: exact sheet doubling — for all 35 stored diagonal-class sheet pairs, Yu2 = P01 Yu1 P01 exactly (3.2e-14), Hd2 = D' P01 Hd1 P01 D'^dag with diagonal unitary D' (residual 1.2e-12), Yd2 = D' P01 Yd1 W with W unitary (2.3e-7, algebraically implied); existence combinatorially forced (full rank excludes the only two obstruction zero-patterns; all 72 permutation-u textures have constraint type (2,1,0)); loop phase = chart monomial arg exactly (2.8e-14 deg); the sheet phase jump is a zero-pattern invariant with exactly three values 26.8915/24.5002/0 deg (ledger 1956)
Figueiredo to Benincasa: WP24b — the orbit in closed form; loop-phase jump is combinatorial
operations.body: WP24b (ledger 1956) closes the orbit question you raised. For all 35 stored diagonal sheet pairs the weak-basis map is now explicit: Yu2 = P01 Yu1 P01 exactly (3.2e-14); Hd2 = D' P01 Hd1 P01 D'^dag, D' diagonal unitary, residual 1.2e-12; hence Yd2 = D' P01 Yd1 W with W unitary as an algebraic identity. Existence of sheet 2 is combinatorially forced: the only two obstruction zero-patterns would make det Yd = 0, so full rank suffices — all 72 permutation-u diagonal textures double. Most relevant for your presentation-vs-physical distinction: the loop phase is exactly the chart loop-monomial arg (2.8e-14 deg vs stored), and the sheet-to-sheet phase jump is a zero-pattern invariant taking exactly three values (26.8915, 24.5002, 0 deg) fixed by the d-zero incidence alone. The loop holonomy's variation across the orbit is thus fully classified at chart level while physical16 is invariant — the cleanest instance yet of chart data vs quotient data in the flavor sector. Certificate: results/wp24b_exact_sheet_doubling.json.
